title: Three guards locate a function with next() and never check it is the only one
summary: Each of the three source-reading guards does next(n for n in ast.walk(...) if it is a FunctionDef named X). Python binds the LAST top-level definition of a name; ast.walk yields the FIRST. So a duplicate definition placed earlier in the file becomes the guard's target while the real one is what runs, and the guard reports on code nobody executes.
next_action: FOUND BY TASK-332's ROUND-2 V4 AND PASSED AS A FINDING RATHER THAN A FAILURE, on reasoning I agree with: the hole needs DEAD CODE NO AUTHOR WRITES -- a duplicate top-level def -- whereas round 1 of TASK-332 broke on INNOCENT edits, which is a different severity; the next(...) formulation is verbatim what TASK-332's own round-1 reviewer prescribed as the fix; and it is a three-site project pattern, one of which is TASK-331's guard that the same reviewer had passed 5 of 5. So the pattern was blessed twice before anyone tested it. THE MECHANISM, exactly: Python binds the LAST top-level definition of a name, ast.walk yields the FIRST. Plant a duplicate 'def summary_shape' earlier in the module carrying both rule literals and a padded register, then delete the real register in full -- ALL 3,253 TESTS GREEN. The round's claim that 'no edit anywhere else in the module can move the target' is therefore false. THE THREE SITES, which I confirmed: tests/test_row_integrity.py:616, tests/test_summary_is_asked_for.py:286 and :347. TWO ONE-LINE FIXES THE REVIEWER VERIFIED: assertEqual(len(fns), 1) after collecting all matches, or read lib.summary_shape.__doc__ off the imported object and drop ast entirely -- the second removes the class of defect rather than guarding against it, and is worth arguing for. WHAT NOT TO BREAK: the nested, conditional, decorator and async attacks all FAIL to defeat these guards today, because ast.walk is breadth-first so a real depth-1 definition always wins. A fix that changes that behaviour has traded one hole for another. ONE MORE THING THE REVIEWER MEASURED: the emptiness floor on the register overclaims -- replacing the whole register with a token line plus 720 characters of the letter x passes it. The floor establishes that the register is LONG, not that it is prose, and the docstring should say so.

A user following the help text can therefore redden the suite permanently in one invocation. ROOT CAUSE IS ONE ASYMMETRY: bin/perry-task:2797 takes the lane from the CALLER, while the importer hardcodes LINKAGE_IMPORT_ACTOR. So the same field is caller-supplied on one path and a constant on the other, and the test that TASK-279 round 2 scoped to actor == goals reads it as if only the importer could ever write it. The V4 measured --actor agent against --actor goals and THE KR COUNTER SCORES THEM IDENTICALLY AT 100 PERCENT, with no disagreement anywhere. So the scope is pinned by mutation but its stated reason does not hold, which is why this row exists rather than a note on TASK-279. WHAT TO DECIDE: either the lane on a linkage record is not caller-supplied -- the writer stamps the lane it IS, the way the importer does -- or the assertion stops keying on a field a caller controls. Do not fix it by refusing --actor with --kr alone; that leaves the same field caller-supplied everywhere else it is stamped.

title: a hand-measured zero and a template zero nobody touched are the same payload, and asserted_at empty is the whole signal
summary: ASKED BY AIMARK 2026-09-09. CONFIRMED BY THE PMO AGAINST THE SCHEMA RATHER THAN AGREED: current_provenance.state is a TWO-VALUED vocabulary, asserted / unasserted, with measured as a separate boolean, and schema/goals-list-contract.md line 143 documents asserted_at empty as 'a real state and not an error: nobody wrote the date down'. So there is no third state available and the empty date is indeed the whole signal. THE CASE AIMARK BUILT IT ON: P003-O2-KR1 carries target 0, current 0, provenance asserted with measured false and asserted_at empty. Its metric prose says the number was measured by hand on 2026-09-07 and shows the grep that produced it, so the zero is real and hard-won -- and the payload's account of it is byte-identical to what a zero nobody ever touched looks like. THIS IS THE SECOND HALF OF THE DEFECT CONTRACT 2.1 ALREADY NAMED AND ONLY HALF-CLOSED. 2.1's note says the register template pre-fills current 0 so a drive-to-zero KR 'reads as achieved on the day it is written', and P002-O2-KR2 did exactly that; current_provenance and current_staleness shipped as the answer. They answer 'is this number stale' and they do not answer 'did anyone ever write this number'. The contract page even says an ABSENT current is null and unasserted, never 0 -- which is the right rule and is not what the template does. WHAT AIMARK DID ON ITS OWN SIDE, so this row does not re-litigate it: krProgress used to return null on any zero target to dodge a division; it now reads target 0 with current 0 as MET, because two numbers were stated and they agree, which is the same reading as target 3 current 3 and not a division at all. A zero target with a NON-zero current still returns null deliberately -- a count that went from four to one is three quarters done only if you know it started at four, and that baseline lives in metric prose. If Perry wants that bar drawn, the baseline has to become a field. DEPENDENCY ADDED 2026-09-10: waits on TASK-415, and this one IS logical as well as practical. TASK-415 establishes the principle in the contract page's own words -- a payload that publishes a measured number with nothing to place it against hands the consumer a value whose only honest rendering is nothing. THIS ROW IS THE SAME PRINCIPLE APPLIED TO THE ZERO CASE: a hand-measured zero and an untouched template row are byte-identical, so a consumer cannot tell a finished KR from one nobody ever wrote. Landing 415 first gives this row the vocabulary to be written in rather than inventing a second way to say the same thing on the same page. Both are minors on schema/goals-list-contract.md, so the changelog-renumbering argument applies here too.

summary: With ids minted, okr.objectives[].id stops being absent and is filled from the store, and the published contract moves to 2.2 with its Not here section rewritten. This row fills okr.objectives[].id, which is a value-meaning change under the 2.2 precedent -- no key moves and the same key returns something different. TASK-415 adds the rule that a measured current may not carry a null target, which is a semantics entry on the same page. Whichever lands second has to renumber its minor and rewrite its changelog row, and two rows editing one changelog concurrently is how a version ends up claimed twice. TASK-415 goes first because it is the smaller change -- data plus one documented rule, no code -- and because aiMark is blocked on it TODAY: its page renders nothing for the most rigorously measured KR in the register. NO LOGICAL DEPENDENCY EXISTS BETWEEN THEM: 415 is about key results, this row is about objectives, and neither reads the other's field. If the sequencing stops mattering -- 415 lands, or is dropped -- this edge should be cut rather than waited on.

title: perry-diagnose reads the whole board line for the word answered, so an ask whose question contains resolved counts as answered
summary: FOUND 2026-09-10 AND IT IS RED ON MAIN RIGHT NOW. bin/perry-diagnose:335 ANSWERED = re.compile(r'\b(answered|resolved|closed|done|decided|已回答|已解决|已决定)\b') is searched against the WHOLE BOARD LINE, so any of those words appearing in the QUESTION marks the ask answered. Measured on USER-924, filed today: its text contains 'round 6, the PAIRING resolved each expectation through the very path it was checking', diagnose matches 'resolved', and open_decisions_by_register.queue reports 0 while one ask is pending. THIS IS TWO IMPLEMENTATIONS OF ONE RULE, the shape this repository keeps finding in itself. viewer/parsers.py:2094 already has _ASK_STILL_OPEN = ('pending','waiting','open','—','-') and ask_is_answered(status_cell) at :2097, which reads the STATUS CELL. perry-diagnose does not call it and scans prose instead -- which ADR-007 decision 3 forbids in as many words: Python does not parse document semantics. IT HAS BEEN BROKEN THE WHOLE TIME AND NOTHING COULD SEE IT. The reconciliation test asserts diagnose and perry-task agree, and 0 == 0 held for weeks because every ask in the queue was answered. It went red the first time a pending ask existed. That is not a flaky test; it is a test that finally got an input. NOTE THE SECOND-ORDER RISK: the fix must not simply widen the regex. Perry-task writes 'pending' and the fixture writes 'open', and the shared predicate already knows both -- calling it is the fix; teaching a second copy the same words is how there come to be three.

That is the shape review.md asks for -- a measured, listed remainder rather than an open search.

title: no test compares a --compact or --json value against the store files or the schema, so a wrong build() agrees with itself
summary: THE READING THE USER DID NOT TAKE ON USER-924, filed so it is a decision with a home rather than an assumption. TASK-362 asked what independent source of truth the --compact projection test has. MEASURED ANSWER: none. tests/test_compact_payload.py reads no store file and no schema -- grep for config.jsonl, okr.jsonl, linkage.jsonl and state-schema returns nothing. --json is the reference on both sides of every comparison in that module, and BOTH payloads come from one build(). If build() reads the wrong source for a field, the two agree, the standup shows the wrong number, and every test in the module passes. THE USER CHOSE READING 1 -- a projection is checked for consistency over its declaration, and the value underneath belongs to the function producing it -- ON A FACT THAT MAKES THIS ROW SMALLER THAN IT LOOKS: --json is already pinned to the schema by a different module, tests/test_wip_and_stages.py:40, and round 7 measured the composition holding (default_stages_for returning [] is green on the compact module and red on the full suite). SO THIS ROW IS NOT 'the payload is unverified'. It is: the pinning is by composition across modules and nobody has enumerated which sections are covered that way and which are not. The deliverable is that enumeration plus a pin for whatever it finds bare -- not a rewrite of the projection tests, which reading 1 settles. CORRECTION 2026-09-10, TO THE CITATION THIS ROW AND USER-924'S ANSWER BOTH REST ON. Both say --json is pinned to the schema at tests/test_wip_and_stages.py:40. That line binds SCHEMA = json.loads(state-schema.json) AND NOTHING EVER READS IT -- grep returns one hit, the assignment. The pin that actually exists is at :83, :90 and :96: a HAND-WRITTEN copy of the queue vocabulary inside the test bodies. THE DECISION IS UNAFFECTED and the composition still holds -- round 8 truncated default_stages_for at bin/perry-state:543 and test_a_blank_stages_cell_reports_the_modes_vocabulary went red, which is what USER-924's reading 1 rests on. BUT THE DIFFERENCE IS REAL AND BELONGS IN THIS ROW: a hand-written vocabulary is a second author, which is the right shape and is why it catches the mutation -- and it is NOT a read of the schema, so it can drift from the schema without anything noticing. That is a narrower guarantee than the one the decision was recorded against, and it makes this row's enumeration more valuable rather than less: whoever does it should count how many sections are pinned by a schema READ versus by a hand-written copy, because those two are not the same promise.

title: perry-diagnose reads the append-only journal as a live reference, so one mistyped id dirties a project forever
summary: FOUND 2026-09-11, AND THE FIRST READING OF IT WAS WRONG -- read the whole entry, the correction is the point. WHAT STARTED IT: test_diagnose.TestUserLoadFindings.test_perry_itself_passes_its_own_id_checks went red on Perry's own project at 7f43a11c, reporting user_load.dangling == ['USER-920']. USER-920 is cited in TASK-281's Next action and has no row anywhere; neighbours 918, 919, 921 and 922 all have one, and git log -S finds no commit where 920 did. ISOLATED BY REMOVAL on scratch copies: replacing the journal's mention clears the finding, replacing only the .perry/events.jsonl mention does not. The journal line is what trips it. THE FIRST CONCLUSION, NOW REFUTED: that the project was PERMANENTLY dirty, because the journal is append-only and USER-920 can never be minted again (a probe filing a row produced USER-926). It is not permanent. Four hours later, same code, the finding was gone. Isolated again, one state file at a time: swapping in the day's journal ALONE clears it. Then the three obvious candidates were each excluded by probe -- deleting the second USER-920 mention from that journal leaves it green, deleting TASK-436's own row leaves it green, and the merges since 7f43a11c touch no code perry-diagnose runs. SO THE REAL DEFECT IS WORSE AND DIFFERENT: THE VERDICT MOVES WITH UNRELATED CONTENT ELSEWHERE IN THE JOURNAL. Same code, same dangling id, same citation, and the answer flips because other lines were written. A guard whose verdict changes when you write something unrelated is not a guard, and it cannot be used as a gate in either direction -- a green run proves nothing and a red one names the wrong cause. THE ROW MUST FIND WHAT ACTUALLY DECIDES IT, which this entry deliberately does not guess at, and then decide what a reference is: a journal is history, and an id cited in a record of what happened on a Tuesday is not a claim that the id exists now. If history stays in the domain, the check needs a remedy a project can perform.
next_action: PART 1 DONE, PART 2 NOT. The harvest path is closed and merged at 9c30782a: any markdown table row's first cell was a definition point, so TASK-436's own spec defined USER-920 and silenced the finding. dangling_in_reports had the same root and went 6 to 80. WHAT IS LEFT is the round's own withdrawal: it enumerated nine append shapes after the PMO showed a case the fix misses, FOUR still move the verdict and this fix closes ONE. (1) work/reference/review-constraints.md already forbids git checkout / stash / reset / clean by name, and the reasoning transfers verbatim -- each one can destroy work that is not yours and not recoverable.
